# pipez: hardening input validation (change on top of pipez/53e6dd6c7354)

## Scope
This is a small change to an existing, working repo. Only three kinds of file change:
- `src/app.js` (wiring)
- a new pure helper `src/validate.js`
- the existing test files `test/app.test.js` and `test/app-module.test.js`

The README API section is also updated. Nothing else in the repo is touched.

## Components and data flow
1. **Request path (unchanged order).** The request passes through the per-app express-rate-limit instance (60 req / 60 s / socket IP, 429 JSON with Retry-After), then `express.json({limit:'10kb'})`, then the routes. `x-powered-by` stays off.
2. **`POST /shorten`** calls `validateUrl(req.body)` from `src/validate.js`. The checks run in this order:
   - (a) The body must be a non-null, non-array object whose `url` is a non-empty string. Otherwise the result is `invalid_url`.
   - (b) If `url.length > 2048` (JS UTF-16 length of the raw string), the result is `url_too_long`. This check runs before any parsing.
   - (c) If the URL contains any ASCII control character, DEL, or any whitespace (`/[\u0000-\u001F\u007F\s]/`), the result is `invalid_url`.
   - (d) The raw string must start with `http://` or `https://` (case-insensitive). This blocks `http:example.com`, which `new URL` would otherwise accept. It also blocks bare hosts, `//host`, `javascript:`, `data:`, `ftp:` and `file:`.
   - (e) `new URL(url)` must not throw. `protocol` must be `http:` or `https:` and `hostname` must be non-empty. Otherwise the result is `invalid_url`.
   - On success, the original string is stored as given. It is not trimmed or normalised.
   - The insert, the 5-attempt collision retry, the 201 shape `{code, shortUrl, url}` and BASE_URL handling are all unchanged.
3. **Malformed JSON.** A body-parser error of type `entity.parse.failed` returns 400 `{"error":"invalid_url"}`. `entity.too.large` still returns 413 exactly as before. Because 2048 < 10kb, 413 and url_too_long never conflict.
4. **`GET /healthz`** stays registered before `GET /:code`. `healthz` is itself 7-character base62, so this order must be kept.
5. **`GET /:code`** checks `isValidCode(req.params.code)` from `src/codes.js` (`/^[0-9A-Za-z]{7}$/`). If the check fails, or the code is not in the DB, the response is 404 `{"error":"not_found"}` with no Location header. A known code returns a 302.
6. **Malformed percent-encoding.** Express 4 decodes route params with `decodeURIComponent`. On a bad sequence such as `/%E0%A4%A` it calls `next(err)` with a 400 URIError before the handler runs. The app's final error handler therefore maps the following to 404 `{"error":"not_found"}`:
   - `err instanceof URIError`, or
   - `err.status === 400` on a GET or HEAD whose `err.type` is not a body-parser type.

   It never returns 500 and never redirects in this case. All other errors keep their existing behaviour.

## Key decisions and how each is honoured
- **deployment.vm_access = live-deploy.** After integration and green tests, pipez or the operator runs the unchanged `deploy/deploy.sh` with DEPLOY_HOST, DEPLOY_USER and DEPLOY_SSH_KEY. It replaces src/ on the VM, restarts the `pipez` unit and keeps `/var/lib/pipez`. Only the literal `DEPLOY OK: http://HOST:3000/healthz -> 200 {"status":"ok"}` line counts as VM verification. If a value is missing or the deploy fails, report NOT RUN or FAILED with the exit code. Never invent a host or credentials. Optional post-deploy smoke test: POST `javascript:alert(1)` returns 400 invalid_url, and GET `/abc` returns 404 not_found. These requests count against the deploying IP's rate limit. The build sandbox cannot reach the VM, so no task runs the deploy.
- **hosting.target: same systemd setup and /healthz.** `deploy/pipez.service`, `provision.sh` and `deploy.sh` are not modified, and `/healthz` is unchanged.
- **network.exposure = direct-port-3000.** No TLS and no proxy. TRUST_PROXY stays unset.
- **legal.license = MIT.** LICENSE is untouched.
- **repo.hosting_ci = none.** No CI files are added.
- **No new dependencies.** Tests use node:test, node:assert/strict and global fetch, with an in-memory DB, in the existing files. No telemetry and no auth.
- **Brief assumptions adopted.** Malformed JSON returns invalid_url. The length check runs before the scheme check. Length is the JS `.length` of the raw string.

## The `deploy` block
The `deploy` field describes a foreground run of `node src/server.js` on a clean Ubuntu reviewer host at `/opt/pipez`. It is NOT the systemd VM. Never run it on the VM that hosts the `pipez` unit, because both bind port 3000.

## Honest "not verified" items for the final report
Unless they are actually run, report these as not verified:
- Docker build and run
- `shellcheck deploy/deploy.sh`
- the privileged provisioning steps
- the live VM line

## OPTIONS (not built)
- A per-route rate-limit exemption for /healthz.
- A URL deny-list for private or loopback hosts (SSRF-style hardening). The brief only asks for scheme and format checks.

modules.name: validate
modules.purpose: A pure, dependency-free URL validator for POST /shorten bodies. It applies the brief's checks in order.
modules.contract:
CommonJS. Exports `{ validateUrl, MAX_URL_LENGTH }` with MAX_URL_LENGTH = 2048. `validateUrl(body)` returns `{ ok: true, url }` (url is the exact input string, unmodified) or `{ ok: false, error: 'invalid_url' | 'url_too_long' }`. It never throws.

Checks, in order:
(1) body is a non-null, non-array object and `typeof body.url === 'string'` and `body.url.length > 0`; otherwise invalid_url.
(2) `url.length > 2048` gives url_too_long.
(3) `/[\u0000-\u001F\u007F\s]/.test(url)` gives invalid_url.
(4) `!/^https?:\/\//i.test(url)` gives invalid_url.
(5) `new URL(url)` throws, or protocol is not in {'http:','https:'}, or hostname is '': invalid_url.

# pipez: increment for systemd deployment on an Ubuntu VM

This change builds on tag `pipez/c7213225e46a`. The API code under `src/`, the Dockerfile, `.dockerignore`, `docker-compose.yml`, `LICENSE`, `.gitignore`, `package.json`/`package-lock.json` and the 15 existing tests stay **as they are**. A file there is touched only if the verification gate finds a real defect. The new work is a `deploy/` directory with three files, one static test file, and README updates.

## Components
1. **App (frozen)**: `src/*.js` is the Express API. It has POST /shorten, GET /:code (302), GET /healthz (200 `{"status":"ok"}`), express-rate-limit at 60 requests per 60 s per IP held in memory, and better-sqlite3 storage in WAL mode. Config comes from env vars: PORT, DB_PATH, TRUST_PROXY and BASE_URL.
2. **systemd unit** `deploy/pipez.service`:
   - Runs `/usr/bin/node /opt/pipez/src/server.js` with `WorkingDirectory=/opt/pipez`, as user and group `pipez`.
   - Sets `Environment=PORT=3000` and `Environment=DB_PATH=/var/lib/pipez/shortener.db`. TRUST_PROXY is not set, so it defaults to false.
   - Uses `StateDirectory=pipez`, `Restart=on-failure`, and hardening: NoNewPrivileges, ProtectSystem=strict, ProtectHome, PrivateTmp, ReadWritePaths=/var/lib/pipez.
   - Logs go to journald through stdout and stderr.
3. **Provisioner** `deploy/provision.sh`: an idempotent bash script, run as root on the VM. It works through these steps in order: OS check (Ubuntu 22.04 or 24.04) → NodeSource node_22.x apt repo, skipped if Node 22 is already installed → build-essential and python3 → `pipez` system user → /opt/pipez and /var/lib/pipez → copy the app and run `npm ci --omit=dev` → install the unit, daemon-reload, enable and restart → poll /healthz for about 30 s → print a firewall hint.
4. **Deploy wrapper** `deploy/deploy.sh`: runs locally. It takes the host, user and key from arguments or from `DEPLOY_HOST`/`DEPLOY_USER`/`DEPLOY_SSH_KEY`. It copies the app and `deploy/` to a staging directory on the VM (rsync, or scp if rsync is missing), runs `sudo bash <staging>/deploy/provision.sh` over SSH, then requires `curl http://HOST:3000/healthz` to return 200 with a JSON content type.
5. **Tests**: the 15 existing node:test tests, plus a new `test/deploy.test.js` that checks the required unit directives and script properties. It is pure Node, with no tools and no dev dependencies.
6. **Docs**: README.md keeps its existing sections and gains a VM deployment section and warnings.

## Data flow (VM)
Client → TCP 0.0.0.0:3000 over plain HTTP (no proxy, no TLS) → Express app. The rate limiter uses the socket IP because TRUST_PROXY is false. Links are stored in the SQLite file `/var/lib/pipez/shortener.db`, in a directory created and owned through StateDirectory. Logs go to journald.

## Deployment flow
- **Operator path:** run `deploy/deploy.sh HOST USER KEY` on a workstation. It copies files over SSH, runs `sudo provision.sh` on the VM, then checks `curl http://HOST:3000/healthz`.
- **pipez path:** the release tarball is extracted to `/opt/pipez/`. The `deploy` block runs `sudo bash deploy/provision.sh` from that directory. provision.sh notices that its source directory already is /opt/pipez and skips the copy. The start command then starts the systemd service and stays in the foreground following its journal.

## How each brief decision is honoured
- **runtime.language (Node/Express):** the code is unchanged. Node 22 is installed on the VM.
- **storage.database (single SQLite file):** `DB_PATH=/var/lib/pipez/shortener.db`. StateDirectory makes the directory owned by `pipez`. The README states that only one instance may run.
- **security.rate_limit:** unchanged. The README notes that the in-memory counters reset on restart.
- **deployment.packaging:** the Docker files are left untouched, and a separate systemd unit runs Node directly.
- **hosting.target (Ubuntu VM with systemd):** covered by `deploy/pipez.service` and `deploy/provision.sh`.
- **deployment.vm_access (live-deploy):** build tasks run in an isolated sandbox with no network access to the VM, so **no task deploys, uses SSH or checks a live host**. The live deploy and the /healthz check on the VM are done by pipez after integration, using the `deploy` block. The operator can also run `deploy/deploy.sh` with the real host, user and key, which come only from arguments or env vars and are never committed. If no credentials are supplied, the live deploy is reported as NOT RUN, along with what is needed: host, user with passwordless sudo, SSH key path, and port 3000 reachable.
- **deployment.os_version (22.04 and 24.04):** provision.sh reads /etc/os-release and exits with a clear message on any other OS.
- **deployment.node_install (NodeSource apt):** signing key at `/etc/apt/keyrings/nodesource.gpg`, repo `https://deb.nodesource.com/node_22.x nodistro main`. The install is skipped if `node` major version 22 is already present.
- **deployment.provisioning (bash script):** plain bash with `set -euo pipefail`. No Ansible or other tools.
- **network.exposure (direct port 3000):** no proxy or TLS. provision.sh prints `ufw allow 3000/tcp` but never changes the firewall. The README explains that the socket IP is used and that TRUST_PROXY must be set if a proxy is added later.
- **storage.backup (none) and data.retention (forever):** the README warns that the DB is not backed up, can be lost permanently, and grows without limit.
- **repo.hosting_ci (none):** no CI files are added.
- **testing.level (basic):** `npm test` (existing tests plus static deploy checks), `systemd-analyze verify deploy/pipez.service`, and `shellcheck deploy/*.sh` are run in the final gate task. Any tool that is unavailable is reported as such.
- **auth.method (none), legal.license (MIT):** unchanged.
- **observability.telemetry (none):** the scripts contact only deb.nodesource.com, Ubuntu apt mirrors, the npm registry, and the target VM (deploy.sh). npm runs with `--no-audit --no-fund` and `NO_UPDATE_NOTIFIER=1`.

## Assumptions (taken from the brief)
- The app lives in /opt/pipez and the service user is `pipez`.
- The service listens on 0.0.0.0:3000.
- The VM user has passwordless sudo.
- The VM has outbound internet access for apt and npm.
- The firewall is left to the operator.

## OPTIONS (not built)
- A reverse proxy with TLS (would also need TRUST_PROXY to be set).
- A periodic `sqlite3 .backup` timer for the DB file.
- A shared rate-limit store, so several instances could run.
- CI to run npm test, shellcheck and systemd-analyze automatically.

bash provisioning scripts (set -euo pipefail), rsync/scp + ssh + curl for the local wrapper
shellcheck and systemd-analyze for verification (used if available)

   - installs the unit, runs daemon-reload, then enable and restart;
   - polls `http://127.0.0.1:3000/healthz` for up to 30 s;
   - prints a firewall reminder.
3. **README section** 'Deploy to an Ubuntu VM (systemd)', plus an updated OPTIONS list.
4. **`test/deploy.test.js`**: dependency-free node:test checks on the static contents of the unit file and install.sh.

## Data flow on the VM
Client → TCP :3000 (plain HTTP, no proxy) → node `src/server.js` under systemd → better-sqlite3 → `/var/lib/pipez/shortener.db`. Because clients connect directly, rate limiting uses the real socket IP.

## How each decision is honoured
- **deployment.vm_access=live-deploy**: pipez provisions the VM itself and runs the `deploy` spec (target vm, user `etl` with passwordless sudo, NodeSource Node 22, `npm ci`, foreground `node src/server.js`, port 3000, `/healthz`). No task touches a host. No SSH, Ansible or remote tooling and no SSH details appear in the repo. install.sh never hardcodes `etl`; it works under any sudo-capable user.
- **hosting.target**: Docker stays as it is, and the VM target is added through the systemd unit and install.sh.
- **os_version 22.04/24.04**: install.sh reads /etc/os-release, requires ID=ubuntu and VERSION_ID in {22.04, 24.04}, and otherwise exits non-zero with a clear message.
- **node_install=nodesource-apt**: the key goes to /etc/apt/keyrings/nodesource.gpg, the source line is `deb [signed-by=...] https://deb.nodesource.com/node_22.x nodistro main`, and `apt-get install -y nodejs` follows.
- **provisioning=bash-script**: a single script with no configuration-management tool.
- **network.exposure=direct-port-3000**: there is no TLS or proxy and TRUST_PROXY stays unset. install.sh does not change the firewall. It prints a reminder, and if ufw is active it prints `sudo ufw allow 3000/tcp` without running it.
- **storage.backup=none and data.retention=forever**: the README says so explicitly. install.sh never deletes /var/lib/pipez.
- **MIT, no telemetry, no auth, SQLite single file, Node+Express, no CI**: unchanged. The tests assert that install.sh contains no telemetry, ssh or ansible references.
- The **existing 15 tests** keep passing, and the new tests are added in a separate file.

## Note on the deploy spec versus the systemd unit
pipez's own deploy runs `node src/server.js` in the foreground as `etl` from `/opt/pipez`, with `DB_PATH=/var/lib/pipez/shortener.db` (directory created and chowned to the deploy user by install_commands). This does not conflict with the unit, which an operator installs separately with `sudo bash deploy/install.sh`. The deploy spec deliberately does not run install.sh, because that would bind port 3000 through systemd and clash with the foreground start_command.

## OPTIONS (not built)
- Optionally run shellcheck on install.sh if it is available locally. It is not added as a dependency.
- Possible later work: a reverse proxy with TLS, a backup timer and a link-retention job.

modules.name: deploy
modules.purpose: Holds the systemd unit and the idempotent Ubuntu install script that deploy pipez as a systemd service with Node 22 from NodeSource.
modules.contract:
FILES OWNED: deploy/pipez.service, deploy/install.sh (git mode 100755).

**pipez.service** must contain these exact lines:
- `[Unit]` with `Description=pipez URL shortener`, `After=network-online.target` and `Wants=network-online.target`.
- `[Service]` with:
  - `Type=simple`, `User=pipez`, `Group=pipez`, `WorkingDirectory=/opt/pipez`
  - `ExecStart=/usr/bin/node src/server.js`
  - `Environment=PORT=3000`, `Environment=DB_PATH=/var/lib/pipez/shortener.db`, `Environment=NODE_ENV=production`
  - `Restart=on-failure`, `RestartSec=2`, `StateDirectory=pipez`
  - `NoNewPrivileges=true`, `ProtectSystem=strict`, `ReadWritePaths=/var/lib/pipez`, `PrivateTmp=true`
- `[Install]` with `WantedBy=multi-user.target`.
- No TRUST_PROXY line.

**install.sh**:
- Line 1 is `#!/usr/bin/env bash`. The first non-comment command is `set -euo pipefail`.
- If EUID != 0 it re-execs itself with sudo: `exec sudo -E bash "$0" "$@"`. It never names a specific invoking user.
- REPO_ROOT is `$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)`.
- It sources /etc/os-release. If ID is not ubuntu, or VERSION_ID is not 22.04 or 24.04, it prints `Unsupported OS: ... (supported: Ubuntu 22.04, 24.04)` to stderr and exits 1.
- It sets `DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive`.
- It runs `apt-get install -y ca-certificates curl gnupg build-essential python3`.
- If `node -v` does not start with `v22.`, it:
  - creates the directory /etc/apt/keyrings with mode 0755;
  - pipes `curl -fsSL https://deb.nodesource.com/gpgkey/nodesource-repo.gpg.key` into `gpg --dearmor --yes -o /etc/apt/keyrings/nodesource.gpg`;
  - writes `deb [signed-by=/etc/apt/keyrings/nodesource.gpg] https://deb.nodesource.com/node_22.x nodistro main` to /etc/apt/sources.list.d/nodesource.list;
  - runs apt-get update, then `apt-get install -y nodejs`.
- It creates the user `pipez` if missing with `useradd --system --home-dir /var/lib/pipez --shell /usr/sbin/nologin --user-group pipez`.
- It runs `install -d -o pipez -g pipez -m 0750 /var/lib/pipez` and `install -d /opt/pipez`.
- It copies the app by staging only package.json, package-lock.json, src/, LICENSE and README.md from REPO_ROOT into /opt/pipez. Stale src is replaced (rm -rf /opt/pipez/src first). Database files, node_modules and .git are never copied. /var/lib/pipez is never removed.
- It runs `cd /opt/pipez && npm ci --omit=dev --no-audit --no-fund`, then `chown -R root:root /opt/pipez` (readable by pipez).
- It installs the unit with `install -m 0644 "$REPO_ROOT/deploy/pipez.service" /etc/systemd/system/pipez.service`, then runs `systemctl daemon-reload`, `systemctl enable pipez` and `systemctl restart pipez`.
- It polls `curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1:3000/healthz` once a second for up to 30 tries. On success it prints OK. On failure it prints `journalctl -u pipez -n 50 --no-pager` and exits 1.
- It prints a reminder that TCP port 3000 must be reachable. If `ufw status` reports active, it prints (does not run) `sudo ufw allow 3000/tcp`.
- It contains none of these substrings (case-insensitive): ssh, ansible, telemetry, analytics.
- It passes `bash -n`.

TESTED BY: test/deploy.test.js (static checks) and `bash -n deploy/install.sh`.
